Maria: Quick sync: we need a concise fallback priority matrix for tenants that require data residency but where catastrophic outages might force degradation. Goal: minimize legal exposure while keeping 99.9% SLOs. Thoughts?

Ajay: Id propose three policy tiers: MUST_RESIDENCY (no cross-region spill ever), RESIDENCY_PREFERRED (prefer local, allow failover to consented region), BEST_EFFORT (route for latency/cost).

Lee: Consent-region needs explicit mapping per tenant (e.g., tenant_jurisdiction=EU -> consent_regions=[eu-west-1, eu-central-1]). We should expose it as header: `X-Residency-Policy: preferred=eu;hard=false;consent=eu-central-1`.

Maria: Also need tenant-tier gating. For enterprise tenants we should gate cross-region fallbacks behind a human-approval w/ timebox; for self-serve, auto-fallback ok if low qps.

Ravi: Human-in-loop is expensive and blows SLOs. Suggest automatic fallback when projected latency > SLA and traffic < X rps, otherwise page on-call.

Sarah: Telemetry to emit: residency.fallback_attempt, residency.fallback_success, residency.fallback_reason, residency.time_to_fallback, residency.legal_exposure_alert. Alert if MUST_RESIDENCY fallback_rate > 0.05% in last 1h.

Ajay: Example minimal config for a tenant: `{"policy":"RESIDENCY_PREFERRED","preferred_region":"eu-west-1","consent_regions":["eu-central-1"],"approval_required":false}`

Lee: Cache semantics: if we route to non-local region we must either namespace caches by region+residency flag or purge keys marked residency-scoped. Otherwise we risk leaking or serving stale constrained data.

Maria: Implementation idea: include a `residency-checksum` in responses and attach `X-Served-Residency: eu-west-1` header. Client and console can verify served location.

OpsBot: Sim run: 3-zone eu outage -> using preferred-fallback matrix served 99.91% locally, 0.07% consent-region, 0.02% failed. Link: https://internal/sim/170334.

Ravi: Billing/cost: cross-region fallback should flag egress and model-hosting uplift. Console should show per-tenant emergency-fallback cost estimates and cumulative monthly impact.

Sarah: Policy enforcement interface: runtime returns structured reason codes (e.g., RESIDENCY_BLOCKED, RESIDENCY_FORCED_FAILOVER). Those should feed into our evals/alerts.

Ajay: Open question: how to represent combined constraints (residency + encryption SSE/HSM). If a tenant requires on-prem KMS, cross-region fallback should be disallowed. We need a constraint matrix.

Lee: Dev note: operator tools will need a dry-run toggle so we can simulate fallback without actually routing traffic. Very useful for legal signoff.

Maria: Action items: (1) Ajay -> draft RFC + JSON schema for tenant residency policy, (2) Lee -> cache namespacing PR + invalidation plan, (3) Sarah -> telemetry + alerting spec, (4) Ravi -> ops runbook stub and emergency-cost model, (5) Ops -> add dry-run flag to runtime.

Ajay: Ill open the RFC and initial schema PR today and tag legal + billing for review.

Maria: Thanks. If anyone cares to be on the enterprise approval list ping me and Ill add you.
